First listed: 2026-06-01 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

- [YouTube: The AI All-You-Can-Eat Buffet Is Ending with Gary Marcus | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 62](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NRSvQqG6BgE) - 2026-06-01
- [Substack: The AI All-You-Can-Eat Buffet Is Ending with Gary Marcus | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 62](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/the-ai-all-you-can-eat-buffet-is) - 2026-06-01

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman maps AI beneficiaries, software risks, financing concentration and physical bottlenecks before interviewing Gary Marcus. Marcus accepts useful coding and brainstorming while emphasizing reliability limits, tool-driven progress and uncertain unit economics. Eisman questions profitable demand rather than treating failure to achieve AGI as sufficient evidence of a bubble, and declines an immediate short despite concern. Several supporting claims require correction or restraint, especially CPU ratios, automatic private-valuation losses and speculation about Anthropic's compute discount.

Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

## Framework and tools

- Separate useful specialized AI from AGI claims.
- Analyze a model together with its tools and verification environment.
- Trace revenue, compute cost, funding and customer concentration separately.
- Differentiate announced capacity from paid utilization.
- A bubble thesis needs a mechanism and catalyst, not just high spending.
- Test price elasticity when subsidized usage becomes metered.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- AI supply-chain map.
- Hyperscaler capex and free cash flow.
- CPU/GPU architecture and power constraints.
- Token and agent cost accounting.
- SpaceX-Anthropic contract terms.
- AI revenue hurdle model.

## Source cautions

Steve Eisman delivers the opening investment map and interviews Gary Marcus. Marcus supplies technical critiques; Eisman states separate financing risks, willingness to be wrong and reluctance to short current growth.
- Entire supplied public transcript read in two contiguous parts.
- Public episode ends with a premium invitation mid-answer; read_complete refers to the complete supplied public source, not an unavailable premium continuation.
- Guest is Gary Marcus. His technical and economic assertions are not automatically Eisman predictions.
- Intro conflates CPU and memory; later question confuses inference with internet retrieval and is corrected by the guest.
